text:
There isn’t one best account for every sole trader or small business in the UK. For most people paid mainly by bank transfer, **Starling** is the strongest everyday choice. If free accounting software matters more than banking features, **Mettle** is often better value.

Fees and limits change, so check the provider’s own pages before you apply.

### Quick picks

| If you mainly need… | Strong option | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Free, full digital banking | **Starling Business** | £0 monthly fee, unlimited free UK transfers, FSCS protection, accounting integrations |
| Free bookkeeping software | **Mettle** (NatWest) | £0 account plus FreeAgent included if you use the account |
| Polished app / cheap cash deposits | **Monzo Business Lite** | Free plan, free UK transfers, cash deposits often £1 each |
| A high-street bank and branches | **HSBC Small Business Banking** | No monthly fee and free UK digital payments; cash is expensive |
| Startup free period + FreeAgent | **NatWest** | Introductory free banking and FreeAgent while you hold the account |

### Starling — best default for most sole traders

Starling is a UK bank with **no monthly fee** and free Faster Payments, Direct Debits and standing orders. Eligible deposits are FSCS-protected (limit is now **£120,000** per person, per banking licence). It connects to Xero, QuickBooks and FreeAgent, and you can deposit cheques.  

The catch is cash: Post Office deposits cost **0.7% or £3, whichever is higher**, and there are daily and annual limits. If you rarely bank cash, the account can genuinely cost nothing. International payments and some extras are charged.  

### Mettle — best if you want FreeAgent free

Mettle is NatWest’s app-based account. It is also free, with free UK transfers, and FSCS cover under NatWest’s licence (so it shares that £120,000 limit with other NatWest Group deposits in your name).  

The standout is **FreeAgent included** — normally about £19 a month for a sole trader — as long as you make at least one transaction a month. That is often worth more than any paid banking tier. Drawbacks: weaker international payments, a narrower product, and cash deposits at the Post Office (commonly cited around **£2.75 per deposit**).  

### Monzo Business — best if you already like the app

**Lite is free**, with free UK transfers and FSCS protection. Monzo often ranks near the top of the CMA business banking service surveys. Cash deposits are relatively cheap (around **£1 per deposit**), which can beat Starling if you pay in cash often. Extra tools and accounting integrations sit mainly on **Pro (£9/month)**. Not available for partnerships or some other structures.

### Tide and the high street

**Tide’s free plan** is fine if you want invoicing in the app and make few transfers (often only a handful free, then about 20p each). Newer accounts are provided via ClearBank, so FSCS cover applies, but the free tier gets expensive if you move money often.

**HSBC’s Small Business Banking Account** has no monthly fee and free standard UK digital payments, plus branches. Cash and cheque handling is charged (around 1.5% on cash, plus per-transaction fees), so it suits people who want a traditional bank and mostly pay digitally, or who may need borrowing.  

**NatWest, Lloyds and Barclays** still suit people who want a branch and an introductory free period (often 12 months, sometimes longer for switchers or start-ups). After that, expect a monthly fee or per-payment charges. NatWest (and RBS) also include FreeAgent with a business account.

### Practical points

- **Sole traders** are not legally required to have a business account, but personal account terms usually ban business use, and a separate account makes Self Assessment, expenses and Making Tax Digital much easier. **Limited companies** must keep company money separate.
- FSCS cover is **£120,000 per person per banking licence**. A sole trader’s business and personal balances at the same bank are added together.
- Cash-heavy trades (markets, salons, trades) should cost the cash fees before choosing an app bank. A high-street free period can be cheaper for a year.
- Restricted sectors (and non-UK-resident directors, for some banks) can be declined. Apply with ID and accurate business details.
- Switching bonuses of £100–£200 appear from time to time on comparison sites such as MoneySavingExpert — worth a quick check, but don’t let a one-off bonus outweigh ongoing fees.

**Practical default:** open **Starling** if you are paid by transfer and want a proper free bank account. Choose **Mettle** if you would otherwise pay for FreeAgent. Use **Monzo Lite** if cheap cash deposits or the Monzo app matter more. Move to HSBC or NatWest if you need a counter, cheques in volume, or borrowing.
